raw_document_text:
# JustiRisk Recidivism Risk Assessment Architecture

## Intended Use and Judicial Role
JustiRisk processes criminal arrest histories, socio-demographic indicators, and court appearance records to output a numerical recidivism risk score (1-10) for arraignment judges.

## Risk Management (Article 9)
A static risk log was produced during initial procurement. Continuous hazard tracking is not integrated into court workflows.

## Data Governance (Article 10)
Training datasets rely on historical county arrest and conviction records spanning 2010-2022.

## Bias Examination & Mitigation (Article 10(2)(f))
Disparate impact analysis and bias mitigation across racial and socioeconomic defendant categories are unaddressed. Systematic false-positive skew against minority defendants is unmitigated.

## Technical Documentation (Article 11)
A vendor summary whitepaper is provided to court administrative officers.

## Automated Logging (Article 12)
Standard database transaction logs record generated scores.

## Transparency & Explainability (Article 13)
Judicial officers receive only the composite risk number. Detailed factor weighting, causal attribution, and algorithmic transparency are absent from the judicial dashboard.

## Human Oversight (Article 14)
Judges retain discretion to depart from recommended risk scores, though no structured operator intervention or fail safe kill switch exists within the software.

## Cybersecurity and Robustness (Article 15)
Basic database access controls are active. Model robustness against data poisoning or missing arrest records has not been systematically validated.
